chunks: And it is narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said:
When the first day of Shawwāl comes, a caller calls out: O believers, go early to your rewards,
Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: O Jābir, the rewards of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are not like the rewards of these kings,
Then he said: It is the Day of Rewards.

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the giver of the true reward
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: the believers being addressed and summoned
key_terms.جَوَائِزِكُمْ: your rewards or prizes from Allah
key_terms.شَوَّالٍ: Shawwāl, the month whose first day is being described
key_terms.مُنَادٍ: a caller who announces the glad tidings
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْجَوَائِزِ: the Day of Rewards, a title for this occasion

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the first day of Shawwāl in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the first day of Shawwāl as a day in which the believers are called toward their divine rewards. It emphasizes that Allah’s rewards are far greater and unlike the gifts of worldly rulers, highlighting the spiritual significance of the day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2060 - It is narrated from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (as), from his father (as), who said:

"When the first day of Shawwal arrives, a caller announces: 'O believers, hasten to your rewards!' Then Abu Ja'far (as) said: 'O Jabir, the rewards of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, are not like the rewards of these worldly kings.'
Then Imam (as) added: 'It is the Day of Rewards.'”
